Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "write a polite email to the ticket desk about exchanging my train booking, please. the booking is for two passengers, on 14 June, from Bellford to North Quay, and cost £36 total. We planned to travel together. i've been given these notes: "Your 08:40 train from Bellford to North Quay is canceled." "The 10:05 service has two seats left, but they are in separate coaches." "Exchanges are free before departure; fare differences may apply." I haven't contacted the desk yet, and I don't know whether the 11:20 train has seats or whether it would cost more. Ask if we can exchange to a service where we can sit together, and specifically whether the 11:20 is an option. If the only available choice is the 10:05 with seats in separate coaches, ask them to confirm that rather than making it sound like we accept it. Also ask whether any fare difference would apply to the possible exchange. Keep the email courteous and fairly concise, and don't make it sound like the exchange has already happened or is guaranteed. There isn't a booking reference or a staff member's name in my notes, so don't make one up.", "output": "Write a polite, fairly concise email to the ticket desk asking about exchanging a train booking. The booking is for two passengers travelling from Bellford to North Quay on 14 June; it cost £36 in total. They planned to travel together and have not yet contacted the desk. Ask whether they can exchange to a service where they can sit together, and specifically whether the 11:20 train is an option. They do not know whether it has seats available or whether it would cost more. If the 10:05 service, with seats in separate coaches, is the only available choice, ask the desk to confirm that rather than implying the passengers accept it. Ask whether a fare difference would apply to a possible exchange. Do not imply that an exchange has already happened or is guaranteed. Do not invent a booking reference or staff member’s name.

Use these notes:
"Your 08:40 train from Bellford to North Quay is canceled."
"The 10:05 service has two seats left, but they are in separate coaches."
"Exchanges are free before departure; fare differences may apply.""}]
